name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,429

clue.text: Thus one African country gets linked with a second one

blocks.note: so means thus, in that way
Mali is a landlocked state in West Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item about one African nation forming ties with a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names one African country in the wordplay and asks for a second as the answer: SO + MALI + A gives SOMALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is another nation on the same continent, in the Horn of Africa, so it is the further country asked for.

clue.text: Will upsets noble, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to shake is to upset or unsettle, and a peer is a noble

explanation.surface: A last testament that unsettles an aristocrat, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a legal document; it is the playwright's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare, the Elizabethan playwright, is commonly known by the short first name Will.

clue.text: Fan of water in shops on American road

blocks.note: a mall is a shopping centre
A is a standard abbreviation for American
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Someone who loves water sports living above the shops on a US street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan of water' sounds like a person; it is a duck, a creature that loves water.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck, a bird that lives on ponds and rivers and so is playfully a lover of wet places.

clue.text: Not entirely vegan girl outside gaming area

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter, the last, is cut from the following word
outside means the girl's name wraps around the shortened word

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
the word vegan with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A girl who eats the odd bit of meat stands outside an arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is the world-famous home of casinos, a city built around gambling.

clue.text: In operation ducks in near back

indicators.note: in places the ducks inside the word for the rear

blocks.note: aft means at or near the back of a ship
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A description of ducks swimming close to the rear of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks are cricket noughts, so two Os; they sit inside AFT to give AFOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is under way or happening, already in progress, as in 'a plan is afoot'.

clue.text: Cold holiday split

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
leave is time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: A chilly break away that left the family divided.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to chop or divide something apart, as with a meat cleaver.

clue.text: Grant including some support offered initially for Edward, say

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of each of the nearby words is used
including means the word for grant holds the selected letters inside it, before its final letter

blocks.note: to confer is to grant or bestow
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A funding award that comes with some upfront help for a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was the English king later made a saint, honoured as a confessor of faith, so he is one example.

clue.text: Make possible overturn of the Spanish prohibition, finally indefensible

indicators.note: to overturn something is to turn it upside down, so in a down entry the following string runs backwards
finally picks out just the closing letter of the next word

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for the
a ban is a prohibition
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A demand that a Spanish ban, being unjustifiable, be struck down to allow something.
explanation.walkthrough: EL + BAN + E read upwards gives ENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to allow or permit something, giving the means for it to happen.

clue.text: Merchant against home payment being raised

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means lifted upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: V is short for versus, against
at home is in
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A trader protesting that the payment on his house is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a wine merchant, a trader who deals in wine.

clue.text: Strange man’s salutation, up here?

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An odd greeting from a man, shouted from a lofty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic 'up here?', a place high above where a greeting might be called down from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas Mountains are a high range in north-west Africa, so a speaker there is literally up at altitude.

clue.text: Manage to avoid publicity - in woman’s clothing?

indicators.note: in, with clothing, means the publicity is dressed in, so wrapped by, the woman

blocks.note: Eve is the first woman, a standard woman's name here acting as the wrapper
an ad, advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A celebrity dodging the press by dressing up as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or dodge something successfully, such as a question or pursuer.

clue.text: With rows featuring unhappily I relented

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things are not in a good state, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words

explanation.surface: Someone who gave in reluctantly after a series of arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels, which fits 'relented'; here it means lines of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-lined avenue has rows of trees along it, so it is characterised by such lines.

clue.text: Stroke play dodge, extremely daring, recollected

indicators.note: extremely takes only the outermost letters, first and last, of the next word
recollected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A batsman recalls a bold shot that was a playful evasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' and 'play' suggest cricket; the stroke is a swimming one.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggy paddle is a simple swimming stroke, paddling the arms beneath the water like a dog.

clue.text: Footman an affected Sir paid to train at first

indicators.note: affected means changed or acted upon, so the letters are altered in their order
at first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grand household where a knight pays to have a servant trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footman' looks like a liveried servant; read it as a man who deals with feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A podiatrist is a foot doctor, a specialist in treating feet, so jokingly a man for the foot.

clue.text: Informative about meat, popular, good

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
veal is calf meat
in means fashionable, popular
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A useful report on a meat dish that is both liked and tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A revealing remark discloses facts, telling you something you did not know before.

clue.text: Self-righteous guy regularly avoiding porridge

indicators.note: regularly avoiding means skipping letters at even intervals, keeping every other one

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious man who never eats oats at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang porridge also means a prison sentence, which deepens the picture of a man too upright to do time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a smug, sanctimonious person who behaves as if morally superior to others.

clue.text: Famous man’s too rich, both detailed

indicators.note: detailed here means having the tail cut off, applied to each of the two words

blocks.note: his means belonging to a man
taken as written, then shortened
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A celebrity whose wealth is so excessive it is itemised.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means important in history, notable or celebrated, as in a historic victory.

clue.text: Distinctive quality of gold noted by artist

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter remarks on the special sheen of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is an atmosphere or air surrounding a person or place, a special character they give off.

clue.text: Having secured somewhere to sleep, girl providing cheese

indicators.note: having secured means holding firmly within, so the girl's name wraps the bed

blocks.note: Rita is a girl's name
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A girl who has found a bed for the night supplies something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey, used in lasagne and cheesecake.

clue.text: Too forceful about right, losing head? My! It gets round!

indicators.note: losing head means the opening letter of the word is removed
the exclamation gets round, so surrounds, the beheaded word, referred to as it

blocks.note: over can mean about, concerning
taken as written
the word right without its first letter

explanation.surface: An excited cry that something domineering has just turned to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for the headless right just described, which goes inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overmighty describes someone with excessive power, too strong for others' good, like an overmighty baron.

clue.text: Very unusual value, saving pounds, after hours

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are shuffled into an unexpected order
after means the jumbled letters come behind the abbreviation for hours

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hours
taken as written
L is pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A rare bargain that saves money, found once the shops have closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' means keeping, so the pounds join the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Helluva is informal slang from 'hell of a', used to mean extremely or very great, as in a helluva shot.

clue.text: Best case to house Military Medal

indicators.note: to house means to give a home inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a suit is a case in law, a lawsuit
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A fine display box for keeping a soldier's decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit is the highest point, the peak or pinnacle of achievement.

clue.text: Retinue with hundred for ultimate in vehement support

indicators.note: with X for Y means one letter takes the place of another in the word
ultimate in means the very last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: an entourage is a retinue of attendants
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A star's followers, swapping a hundred for the last word in passionate backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage is to give support and confidence, to back someone up and urge them on.

clue.text: Bird, black - escaping from hound

indicators.note: escaping from means a letter gets out of, so leaves, the word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a beagle is a hunting hound

explanation.surface: A dark bird fleeing from a hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey with a hooked beak and keen eyesight.

clue.text: City has Lutherans, some heading West

indicators.note: some means part of the letters on show, a run inside the words
heading west in an across entry means going right to left, against normal reading

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A town that has a population of Lutherans, some moving westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma in the United States, on the Arkansas River.

clue.text: Give information about time a politician crushed popular haunt

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses the next ones

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament
ground means crushed into small pieces

explanation.surface: An informer telling of a time when an MP was flattened at a favourite spot.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for telling the police what you know.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamping ground is a place someone habitually visits and frequents, their favourite hangout.

clue.text: Badly organised, intermittently arrange children’s game

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
tag is a chasing game played by children

explanation.surface: A shambolic attempt to set up a playground game now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag means disorderly, untidy or motley, as in a ragtag army of volunteers.

clue.text: In from France warning about lake - area surrounded

indicators.note: about means around, so the warning wraps the abbreviation for lake

blocks.note: en is the French for in
cave, Latin for beware, is a schoolboy warning
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A French notice warning of a lake, in a region hemmed in on all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'kay-vee') is old British public-school slang for 'look out!', from the Latin for beware.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly enclosed within another, such as a small state inside a larger one.
